# Using the Org Atlas authoring agent

<!-- Generated by `npm run agent` from engine/vocab/*.yaml and the JSON Schema. Do not edit by hand. -->

The agent turns a description of your organization into an Org Atlas chart, or changes an existing one. It always matches this repository's vocabulary, because these files are regenerated by `npm run generate`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [org-atlas-agent.md](org-atlas-agent.md) | The full agent: instructions, every kind, field, value and relationship type, and an example |
| [tool.json](tool.json) | A tool / function definition whose input is a valid bundle, for LLM APIs |
| [../.claude/agents/org-atlas-author.md](../.claude/agents/org-atlas-author.md) | The same agent as a Claude Code subagent |

## Quick start in any chat LLM

1. Start a chat and paste the whole of `org-atlas-agent.md` as the first message (or attach it).
2. Describe what you want: "Model our Data and Analytics business unit: three teams, these people, these platforms and who owns them." To change your current chart, first run `npm run export -- --pack --out atlas-pack.json` and attach that file too.
3. Save the JSON block it returns as `data/atlas.json` and run `npm run validate -- data/atlas.json`. Paste any errors back into the chat and ask it to fix them.
4. `npm run dev` to see the result.

## Set it up once

Some tools limit the size of their instruction box. For those, paste the short instructions below and attach `org-atlas-agent.md` as a file.

**Short instructions:**

```text
You are the Org Atlas authoring agent. Your full instructions are in the attached file org-atlas-agent.md: read it before every answer and follow it exactly. You turn descriptions of an organization into one Org Atlas JSON bundle { "atlas": 1, "entities": [...], "relationships": [...] }, or change a bundle or context pack the user gives you and return the complete updated bundle. Use only the kinds, fields, allowed values and relationship types in that file (or in a context pack the user provides). Never invent real people's names. Answer with one short summary line, one json code block with the complete bundle, then a short list of assumptions and warnings.
```

| Tool | Where to put it |
|---|---|
| ChatGPT (custom GPT) | Instructions: the short instructions. Knowledge: upload `org-atlas-agent.md` (and optionally `atlas-pack.json`) |
| Claude (Project) | Project instructions: the short instructions, or the whole of `org-atlas-agent.md`. Project knowledge: `org-atlas-agent.md` and optionally `atlas-pack.json` |
| Gemini (Gem) | Instructions: the short instructions. Knowledge: upload `org-atlas-agent.md` |
| Microsoft Copilot (agent) | Instructions: the short instructions. Knowledge: upload `org-atlas-agent.md` |
| Any LLM API | System prompt: the whole of `org-atlas-agent.md`. Optionally pass `tool.json` as a tool and require it, so the answer is always a valid bundle |
| Claude Code | Nothing to do: ask for the `org-atlas-author` subagent in this repository |
| Codex, Cursor, Copilot in the editor | Nothing to do: they read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), which points here |

After you add custom vocabulary in `overrides/vocab/`, run `npm run generate` and re-upload `org-atlas-agent.md` wherever you attached it.

## Good first requests

- "Here is a list of our teams and who leads them: ... Build the org chart."
- "Snowflake is owned by Data Platform for the warehouse and by Finance Systems for finance data loads. Add that as shared ownership."
- "Add a Center of Excellence for Data and AI chaired by Maria Chen, with these members: ..."
- "Add a churn model inside the Customer Insights product, built with Python and scikit-learn, owned by Data Science."
- "Using this context pack, who supports Kafka and which products would be affected if it went down?"
